The test image shows a banana leaf with:
- Predominant yellow-green coloration with horizontal stripe patterns
- A dark/black lesion visible in the upper right
- Parallel streaking along the leaf veins

This pattern of yellow streaks with dark spots is suggestive of Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka. Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka image shows advanced-stage discrete lesions with yellow halos and dark necrotic centers on a green leaf. The test image looks different — it shows a predominantly yellowed leaf with horizontal banding parallel to the veins and one dark spot.

**Analysis:**
- Test image: diffuse yellow-green coloration, horizontal stripe/banding pattern along veins, one dark spot upper right
- Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka reference: discrete oval lesions with yellow halo + dark center on green background

The test image's inter-veinal yellowing with stripe patterns is consistent with Yellow Sigatoka (an earlier stage where yellow streaks appear between veins before developing into the classic dark necrotic lesions). The horizontal banding exactly matches how Sigatoka progresses — yellow streaks parallel to veins that later turn brown/black.

The other candidates are less likely:
- Panama Disease: causes yellowing from margins inward, not inter-veinal banding
- Bunchy_Top: causes dark green dot-dash streaks and leaf bunching, not diffuse yellowing
- Cordana/Anthracnose/Cigar_End_Rot: affect different plant parts with distinct lesion patterns
